summary.one_liner: hyperfine is a command-line benchmarking tool that times one or more commands with statistical analysis and exports the results.
summary.what_it_does: Runs arbitrary commands repeatedly and reports statistics such as mean, stddev, median, min and max across runs. It supports warmup runs, per-run preparation commands (e.g. cache clearing), setup/conclude/cleanup commands, and parameter scans over numeric ranges or value lists. Metrics include wall-clock time, CPU user/system time, peak resident memory, and hardware counters on Linux and macOS in some cases. Results can be exported to CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc, and org-mode, and the first command serves as the reference for relative comparisons. The README describes outlier detection and shell-startup correction when a shell is used.
use_cases: Compare the speed of two or more command-line programs
Benchmark a shell command with warm or cold disk caches
Scan a program's runtime across a range of parameter values such as thread counts
Measure peak memory and CPU counters of a command
Export benchmark tables to Markdown or JSON for reports
notable: Warmup and per-run prepare commands for cold or warm cache testing
Shell startup time is measured and subtracted when a shell is used
Multiple export formats including Markdown, AsciiDoc, CSV and JSON
Optional hardware counters such as instructions and cache misses on Linux
caveats: Hardware counters are not available when a shell is enabled, and several metrics are unsupported on Windows and macOS
Peak memory on Linux can report an inherited value for very small commands
Rust 1.97 or newer is needed to build from cargo
keywords: how long does a command take
